applicability.scope: Device identity, compat-layer dispatch and pinned-image constraints for text-LLM and Omni serving on the vllm-musa plugin, plus the measurement rules that keep a CUDA-derived result separate from a MUSA one.
applicability.prerequisites: A prepared MUSA host or the vllm-omni MUSA image, the plugin and compat-layer revisions, and a frozen benchmark plus quality command.
applicability.input_contract: Plugin revision, upstream vLLM version, MUSA toolkit and driver, torchada/torch_musa revisions, model checkpoint, physical device UUID set and the workload.
applicability.produced_artifact: An identity/dispatch/measurement report: physical device mapping, the named mechanism and its kernel evidence, and an AB/BA pair with its quality verdict.
applicability.refusal_point: Report an evidence gap when the physical device set, the compat-layer revisions or the image constraint list cannot be established.

recommendations: Resolve the pymtml-physical versus torch-logical device mapping before any A/B.
Prove the mechanism is selected on MUSA from a profile instead of assuming a CUDA fast path ran.
Treat the Omni image's constraint list as the boundary of what can cause a change.
Keep the text-LLM and Omni lanes as separate claims.
limitations: Authored from source reading only: no MUSA hardware run, no quality or performance measurement.
Covers the plugin's contract at one revision; MATE, torchada and MUSA toolkit tuning are out of scope.
Contains no expected speedup and no statement that any CUDA or Ascend record transfers to MUSA.

construction.method: Source-read authoring against the plugin revision recorded in references/sources.md. No MUSA host was available, so no native import, build, service start or measurement was performed.
